# Spec-side black-box experiments (spec side only)

Small images the spec side runs in fwtest to confirm facts in
`docs/HARDWARE-SPEC.md` (M0c). The spec cites them only as E-n and their
result; nothing here leaves `harness/`. They are written from the JieLi
SDK's register map and, where the SDK has no bit meanings, from the vendored
emulator's model (`exp.h` says which). Each confirms how fwtest presents the
board, not how real hardware behaves.

- Build: `sh harness/spec-experiments/build.sh` (the pinned toolchain
  container; writes `images/` and `images/SHA256SUMS`).
- Run: `sh harness/spec-experiments/run.sh OUT` rebuilds, compares with the
  committed images, and runs `experiments.suite` against this checkout's
  fwtest (C-SPEC-EXPERIMENTS, R-SPEC-4). The golden files are the results.
- Not part of fwtest: `harness/ci.sh` leaves this folder out of the fwtest
  build context, and the image-publishing workflow ignores it.

| ID | Image | What it shows (the golden files hold the numbers) |
|----|-------|---------------------------------------------------|
| E-1 | `e1-boot` | At entry: r0 = 0x01C7FC00, r2..r15, sp, usp, ssp, icfg, psr and cnum all 0 (r1 not observable: used as the pointer). The block at r0: first word 0x01C7FC40, the other 15 zero. The code window past the image reads 0xFFFFFFFF (erased flash), also 4 KiB further. A written word reads back at 0x01C7FDFC, 0x01CFFFFC, 0x01F3FFFC and 0x0407FFFC. |
| E-2 | `e2-console` | Word writes to DBG_MSG append their 4 bytes, low byte first. A byte or halfword write appends 4 bytes too: the written bytes merged into the last word written (console "abcd12:\nX2:\nYZ:\nend\n"). |
| E-3 | `e3-timers` | TIMER5 PRD 600: an interrupt (63) every 100 µs; TIMER4 advanced 2400 counts (24 MHz) between two. TIMER0 prescaler index 2, PRD 1500: an interrupt (4) every 1 ms; its CON read in the handler is 0x8021 (bit 15 pending). TTMR with PRD 1234: an interrupt (3) every 10 ms. ILAT_SET bit 0: interrupt 120 once. Counts at 52.3 ms (the capture came late, below): 523, 52, 5, 1. |
| E-4 | `e4-core1` | With core 1's entry in the word at 0x01C7FFF8, setting C1_CON bit 3 starts core 1 there; cnum reads 0 on core 0 and 1 on core 1; core 1 ran on stacks it set itself. |
| E-5 | `e5-lcd` | SPI1 bytes with PC8 low are commands, high data. CASET/RASET/RAMWR with RGB565 pixels high byte first, by single bytes (BUF) and by DMA (ADR, CNT from RAM) both draw. INVON and DISPOFF leave the captured picture as written. A software reset (0x01) clears it to black. |
| E-6 | `e6-matrix` | The log gives each fwtest key's (column, row) and each encoder's two contacts and their order (clockwise: the second contact closes first). Matches the table in the spec. |
| E-7 | `e7-leds` | LED line PA9, PA10, PH6, PH9 lights, in the selected column, the LED of the key at row 1, 2, 3, 4 of that column. |
| E-8 | `e8-adc` | Channel 4 reads the pot (900 at the start, then the script's 300, 0, 1023); channel 3 reads 640; every other channel 512. |
| E-9 | `e9-audio` | A half of 128 words (64 frames) every 1.451 ms after the first at 1.459 ms (44 117.6 frames a second). The first half to finish is half 0; the half just finished is CON0 bit 15 inverted. A sample is the word shifted right by 8, clamped to 16 bits: 0x007fffff gives 32767, 0xff800000 -32768, 0x01000000 32767, 0x00000080 0. |
| E-10 | `e10-faults` | No fault reaches sources 0-2 (handlers count 0), before and after writing EMU_CON 0x001F010F, EMU_SSP/USP limits excluding the stacks, DBG_EN 0x003F0030. Misaligned word loads give the bytes at the address (RAM+1: 0x04030201; code+1: 0x14131211); halfword loads at RAM+1 and +3 give 0x0100 and 0x0302 (the lowest address bit ignored); a word stored at RAM+9 lands in bytes 9-12. The addresses come from a volatile word: with constant addresses the compiler split the RAM accesses into byte accesses. Unmapped 0x00ABCDEC reads 0, and after a write still 0. A code-window write reads back unchanged. Signed and unsigned 1234/0 give 0; 1234%0 (as compiled) gives 1234. EMU_CON and the limits read back; EMU_MSG 0; DBG_EN 0 (unmodelled). The console is "E10\nend\n": writes to DBG_WR_EN and DBG_MSG_CLR between the two words left it alone. |
| E-11 | `e11-undefined` | A call to a function whose first halfword is 0xFFFF: the run ends as a fault ("cannot decode"), after the marker, with no handler run. |
| E-12 | `e12-badjump` | A call to 0x00ABCDEE: fwtest runs the zeros it reads there for 1024 instructions, then ends the run as a fault ("the pc left every memory"); no handler ran. |
| E-13 | `e13-timer-ack` | TIMER0, prescaler index 2, PRD 1500: 100 periods are 2 400 100 TIMER4 ticks with the acknowledge first in the handler (1 tick after entry) and 2 408 160 with it 82 ticks after entry; CNT reads 5 just before the acknowledge, 0 just after. The periphery model restarts the count and the period at every CON write. |
| E-14 | `e14-undefined-inline` | A marker store, then the halfword 0xFFFF in the same straight-line code: the run ends as a fault at the start of that code (the pc of main's first instruction), and the marker was never written. |
| E-15 | `e15-spi1-irq` | SPI1 CON bit 13 and source 16. CON reads 0x8000 before any write. Bit 13 never set, or written clear: no interrupt for a 2-byte DMA or a BUF byte. Bit 13 set: one interrupt each (the handler acknowledges with `CON |= 0x4000`); CON reads 0xA000. A DMA done with bit 13 set and the source off in ICFG, then CON written 0 and the source turned on: taken once. Before the SR-3 fix (vendor patch 0002, fwtest 0.2.0) a CON write could not clear bit 13, so the clear steps counted too. |
| E-16 | `e16-lcd-frame` | One CNT write of 115 200 bytes from RAM draws a whole frame (rows 0-119 red, 120-239 blue), pixel (0,0) green and (239,239) white in place. |
| E-17 | `e17-adc-irq` | SARADC CON bit 5 and source 24: a start of channel 4 with bit 5 gives one interrupt, without it none, also right after one with it. In the handler RES 900, CON 0x4F0; after the acknowledge (CON = 0x40) CON 0x40; after a start without bit 5, 0x4D0. |
| E-18 | `e18-block-moves` | The block moves with a register base, as the pinned toolchain assembles them, all eight modes (`[rN+]`, `[rN++]`, `[-rN]`, `[--rN]`, loads and stores), bases r0, r4 to r11, r13, r15, two to fifteen registers: the lowest register takes the lowest address; `[-rN]` and `[--rN]` take the words just below the base; the base keeps its value except with `++` (base + 4n) and `--` (base - 4n); `{r3, r0} = [-r0]` loads both words from the original base. |

**Late captures.** While core 0 waits (in `idle`, or polling TIMER4), fwtest
takes captures only between its runs of up to 1024 instructions, and each
wait can jump time ahead by up to the next event, so a capture can come
several milliseconds after the time asked (E-3's "10 ms" capture was taken at
14.1 ms). E-5 and E-7 therefore time themselves by busy counting. This is
fwtest behaviour, reported in docs/HARNESS.md ("Time").

/* E-17: the SARADC's interrupt (source 24) and CON bit 5. A handler on
   source 24 counts its entries in OUT(12), keeps RES and CON as read on
   entry in OUT(13), OUT(14), acknowledges by writing CON with bit 6 alone,
   and keeps CON as read just after in OUT(15). Each step starts one
   conversion of channel 4 (the pot) and waits a while:
     0: start (bits 4 and 6) without bit 5;
     1: start with bit 5;
     2: start with bit 5 again;
     3: start without bit 5.
   OUT(2k) is the count after step k and OUT(2k + 1) CON read then. */
#include "exp.h"

#define IRQ_SARADC 24u
#define START ((4u << 8) | 0x10u | 0x40u)

__attribute__((interrupt)) void adc_isr(void)
{
    OUT(12)++;
    OUT(13) = ADC_RES;
    OUT(14) = ADC_CON;
    ADC_CON = 0x40u;
    OUT(15) = ADC_CON;
}

static void keep(u32 k)
{
    for (volatile u32 i = 0u; i < 2000u; i++) {
    }
    OUT(2u * k) = OUT(12);
    OUT(2u * k + 1u) = ADC_CON;
}

int main(void)
{
    VECTOR(IRQ_SARADC) = (u32)adc_isr;
    ICFG(IRQ_SARADC) |= ICFG_ON(IRQ_SARADC, 2u);
    irq_on();
    ADC_CON = START;
    keep(0);
    ADC_CON = START | 0x20u;
    keep(1);
    ADC_CON = START | 0x20u;
    keep(2);
    ADC_CON = START;
    keep(3);
    OUT(16) = 0x600dd00eu;
    return 0;
}

set -eu

inside() {
    out=$1
    cd "$HERE"
    flags="-target pi32v2 -std=c11 -ffreestanding -nostdlib -Os -Wall -Wextra -Werror"
    clang -target pi32v2 -c start.S -o "$out/start.o"
    clang -target pi32v2 -c boot.S -o "$out/boot.o"
    # shellcheck disable=SC2086
    clang $flags -c e1-boot.c -o "$out/e1-boot.o"
    ld -nostdlib -T image.ld -o "$out/e1-boot.elf" "$out/boot.o" "$out/e1-boot.o"
    objcopy -O binary -j .text "$out/e1-boot.elf" "$out/e1-boot.bin"
    for n in $IMAGES; do
        # shellcheck disable=SC2086
        clang $flags -c "$n.c" -o "$out/$n.o"
        ld -nostdlib -T image.ld -o "$out/$n.elf" "$out/start.o" "$out/$n.o"
        objcopy -O binary -j .text "$out/$n.elf" "$out/$n.bin"
    done
    for n in $ASM_IMAGES; do
        clang -target pi32v2 -mcpu=r3 -c "$n.S" -o "$out/$n.o"
        ld -nostdlib -T image.ld -o "$out/$n.elf" "$out/start.o" "$out/$n.o"
        objcopy -O binary -j .text "$out/$n.elf" "$out/$n.bin"
    done
    rm -f "$out"/*.o "$out"/*.elf
    (cd "$out" && for n in e1-boot $IMAGES $ASM_IMAGES; do sha256sum "$n.bin"; done > SHA256SUMS)
}

import os
import unittest

from tests.helpers import ROOT, load_tool

hs = load_tool("check-hardware-spec.py")

GOOD = """# Hardware spec

## 1. Boot

### HW-1: Load address
- Fact: The image starts at the window's first byte.
- Sources: HARNESS ("The raw image"); E-1.
- Standing: confirmed (E-1)
- Needed by: M0d

### HW-2: Something the model says
- Fact: A property, continued
  on a second line.
- Sources: the emulator model.
- Standing: emulator-only
- Needed by: M1

## Open questions

- **Q-1. Clocks.** Not known.
"""


class HardwareSpecLintTest(unittest.TestCase):
    """Requirements: R-SPEC-1, R-SPEC-3"""

    def problems(self, text, base=None, exps=frozenset({"1"})):
        return hs.lint(text, base, set(exps) if exps is not None else None)[1]

    def test_good(self):
        entries, problems = hs.lint(GOOD, None, {"1"})
        self.assertEqual(problems, [])
        self.assertEqual(entries["HW-2"]["Fact"], "A property, continued on a second line.")

    def test_missing_field_and_unknown_field(self):
        bad = GOOD.replace("- Needed by: M1\n", "- Notes: x\n")
        p = self.problems(bad)
        self.assertTrue(any("HW-2" in x and "no Needed by" in x for x in p), p)
        self.assertTrue(any("unknown field 'Notes'" in x for x in p), p)

    def test_empty_source(self):
        p = self.problems(GOOD.replace("- Sources: the emulator model.", "- Sources:"))
        self.assertTrue(any("HW-2" in x and "no Sources" in x for x in p), p)

    def test_duplicate_id_and_question(self):
        p = self.problems(GOOD.replace("### HW-2:", "### HW-1:") + "- **Q-1. Again.** x\n")
        self.assertTrue(any("HW-1 is used twice" in x for x in p), p)
        self.assertTrue(any("Q-1 is used twice" in x for x in p), p)

    def test_standing(self):
        p = self.problems(GOOD.replace("- Standing: emulator-only", "- Standing: probably"))
        self.assertTrue(any("standing 'probably'" in x for x in p), p)
        p = self.problems(GOOD.replace("- Standing: emulator-only", "- Standing: superseded by HW-9"))
        self.assertTrue(any("superseded by HW-9" in x for x in p), p)
        self.assertEqual(self.problems(GOOD.replace("- Standing: emulator-only",
                                                    "- Standing: superseded by HW-1")), [])

    def test_confirmed_needs_an_independent_source(self):
        for weak in ("the emulator model.", 'HARNESS ("The raw image").'):
            bad = GOOD.replace('- Sources: HARNESS ("The raw image"); E-1.', "- Sources: " + weak)
            p = self.problems(bad, exps=None)
            self.assertTrue(any("HW-1: confirmed, but" in x for x in p), (weak, p))

        self.assertEqual(self.problems(GOOD, exps=None), [], "skipped where harness/ is absent")

        p = self.problems(GOOD + "\n```c\nint x;\n```\n")
        self.assertTrue(any("fenced code block" in x for x in p), p)

### HW-67: The FM-1's MIDI inputs, and the one fwtest feeds
- Fact: The FM-1 takes MIDI in three ways, all active at once: a 3.5 mm
  MIDI IN jack carrying serial MIDI at 31 250 baud, USB MIDI (the FM-1 is a
  class-compliant USB device with a MIDI and an audio interface), and MIDI
  over Bluetooth LE. It has no MIDI OUT jack; it sends MIDI over USB and
  Bluetooth only. On the chip, the jack's serial MIDI is received by UART1
  (`JL_UART1`, HW-68), through its receive DMA. fwtest models only the jack:
  a script's `midi` event (HARNESS, "Input scripts") delivers its bytes to
  UART1's receiver, and fwtest has no USB or Bluetooth MIDI. Which pin the
  jack reaches, and how the TRS socket is wired (type A or B), the sources
  don't say (Q-12).
- Sources: MAN (the FM-1's manual, English part, p. 10, "MIDI
  Connectivity": the three interfaces, the jack's 31 250 baud; "What the
  FM-1 sends via MIDI"); RE `docs/io/05-midi.md` §1 and §2 (the three
  transports; UART MIDI on the UART at `0x00012100`, received by DMA),
  `docs/io/06-usb.md` §1 (a USB composite device, audio and MIDI),

  `WL82.h` lines 569-591 (UART1's base); E-19 (fwtest's `midi` bytes reach
  UART1's ring).
- Standing: confirmed (MAN, RE, SDK, E-19)
- Needed by: M6a (SR-8)

- Fact: The chip has three UARTs, `JL_UART0`, `JL_UART1` and `JL_UART2`,
  at `0x00012000`, `0x00012100` and `0x00012200`. Each has the words, from
  its base: `CON0` +0x00, `CON1` +0x04, `BAUD` +0x08, `BUF` +0x0C, `OTCNT`
  +0x10, `TXADR` +0x14, `TXCNT` +0x18, `RXSADR` +0x1C, `RXEADR` +0x20,
  `RXCNT` +0x24, `HRXCNT` +0x28. `CON0`, `CON1`, `BAUD`, `TXCNT` and
  `HRXCNT` are 16 bits and `BUF` 8 bits, each in the low part of its word;
  `BAUD` and `TXCNT` are write-only and `HRXCNT` read-only. Their interrupt
  sources are 19, 20 and 21. A UART's transmit and receive pins are either
  one of its fixed pin pairs, given as transmit then receive (UART1: PH6 and
  PH7, PC3 and PC4, PB3 and PB4, or the USB pins), or any pin, through an
  output and an input channel of the port map (`JL_IOMAP`). The UART clock
  is the low-speed bus clock, the crystal oscillator or the PLL's 48 MHz
  (`CLK_CON1` bits 10-11, HW-53). The SDK's driver receives into a circular
  buffer by DMA, with an interrupt after a given number of bytes and an
  idle timeout counted in clocks, and each of the transmit, receive and
  timeout interrupts can be left off. The SDK gives no bit meanings for
  `CON0`, `CON1` or `BAUD` (its UART driver is a prebuilt library).

  SDK `include_lib/driver/cpu/wl82/asm/uart.h` (three UARTs, the pin pairs,
  the input and output channels); SDK `include_lib/driver/device/uart.h`
  (the clock choices, the circular buffer, the byte count and idle timeout,
  the interrupts that can be left off).
- Standing: confirmed (SDK)
- Needed by: M6a (SR-8)

### HW-69: UART1's receive flags, their acknowledge and the count latch
- Fact: In UART1's `CON0`, read: bit 14 is set when the receive DMA has
  taken the set number of bytes (receive pending), bit 11 when the line has
  been idle for the set time after a byte (timeout pending). Written as 1:
  bit 12 clears the receive pending, bit 10 the timeout pending, bit 13 the
  transmit pending (HW-73); bit 7 latches into `HRXCNT` how many bytes the
  receive DMA has written since the previous latch. A handler for source 20
  reads `CON0`, latches with bit 7, reads `HRXCNT`, and acknowledges the
  pending flags. FM-1's own firmware does this, with no other receive mode.
- Sources: RE `docs/io/05-midi.md` §2.1 (the UART's flags at `0x00012100`:
  `0x4000` receive pending, `0x800` timeout; acknowledged with `0x80`,
  `0x1000`, `0x400`, `0x2000`; the count at `0x00012128` read in the
  handler); E-19 (the same bits in fwtest).
- Standing: confirmed (RE, E-19)
- Needed by: M6a (SR-8)

### HW-70: UART1's receive set-up bits, the ring, the count and the timeout
- Fact: In UART1's `CON0`: bit 0 turns the UART on; bit 2 enables the
  transmit interrupt, bit 3 the receive interrupt (bit 14, HW-69), bit 5
  the timeout interrupt (bit 11); bit 6 turns the receive DMA on. The DMA

  not including, `RXEADR`, and wraps to `RXSADR`; writing `RXSADR` starts

  last latch that sets the receive pending (0: never). `OTCNT` is the idle
  time, in UART clocks (48 MHz from the PLL), after a byte that sets the
  timeout pending. The sources give no receive by `BUF` a byte at a time,
  no error flags (framing, overrun) and no `BAUD` formula (Q-12).

  (that the receive is a DMA ring with a byte count and an idle timeout,
  not the bits); E-19, E-20 (fwtest behaves so).
- Standing: emulator-only
- Needed by: M6a (SR-8)

### HW-71: UART1's receive in fwtest
- Fact: In fwtest a `midi` byte arrives 320 µs after the one before it,
  whatever `BAUD`, `CON1`, `CLK_CON1` and the pins are set to: none needs
  setting. fwtest counts as "a MIDI receiver set up" (HARNESS, `result.json`'s
  `midi_bytes_dropped`) `CON0` with bits 0 and 6 set and `RXEADR` −

  receive pending is set when the bytes since the last latch reach `RXCNT`,

  later byte. The timeout comes `OTCNT` × 5 cycles (at 240 MHz) after the
  last byte, and at least one byte time (320 µs). Source 20 then interrupts
  as any source does (HW-20, HW-22). E-19: with `RXCNT` 4 and `OTCNT`
  48 000, six bytes from 3 ms give a receive pending at 4.28 ms with
  `HRXCNT` 4, and a timeout at 5.92 ms with `HRXCNT` 2.
- Sources: E-19, E-20; HARNESS ("Input scripts", "Outputs").
- Standing: confirmed (E-19, E-20)
- Needed by: M6a (SR-8)

  `0x1000`, `0x400`, `0x2000`; the count at `0x00012128` read in the
  handler); E-19 (the same bits in fwtest).
- Standing: confirmed (RE, E-19)
- Needed by: M6a (SR-8)

### HW-70: UART1's receive set-up bits, the ring, the count and the timeout
- Fact: In UART1's `CON0`: bit 0 turns the UART on; bit 2 enables the
  transmit interrupt, bit 3 the receive interrupt (bit 14, HW-69), bit 5
  the timeout interrupt (bit 11); bit 6 turns the receive DMA on. The DMA
  writes each byte at the next address of the ring from `RXSADR` up to,
  not including, `RXEADR`, and wraps to `RXSADR`; writing `RXSADR` starts
  it again at the ring's start. `RXCNT` is the number of bytes since the
  last latch that sets the receive pending (0: never). `OTCNT` is the idle
  time, in UART clocks (48 MHz from the PLL), after a byte that sets the
  timeout pending. The sources give no receive by `BUF` a byte at a time,
  no error flags (framing, overrun) and no `BAUD` formula (Q-12).
- Sources: the emulator model; SDK `include_lib/driver/device/uart.h`
  (that the receive is a DMA ring with a byte count and an idle timeout,
  not the bits); E-19, E-20 (fwtest behaves so).
- Standing: emulator-only
- Needed by: M6a (SR-8)

### HW-71: UART1's receive in fwtest
- Fact: In fwtest a `midi` byte arrives 320 µs after the one before it,
  whatever `BAUD`, `CON1`, `CLK_CON1` and the pins are set to: none needs
  setting. fwtest counts as "a MIDI receiver set up" (HARNESS, `result.json`'s
  `midi_bytes_dropped`) `CON0` with bits 0 and 6 set and `RXEADR` −
  `RXSADR` from 1 to 65 536. A byte arriving otherwise is dropped and
  counted: no interrupt, nothing in RAM, and `BUF` reads 0; fwtest has no
  receive through `BUF`. So does a byte with more than 3 125 waiting (about
  a second). Received bytes go into the ring as HW-70 says: a byte that
  arrives before the firmware has read the one before is kept; past the
  ring's size the oldest are overwritten, with no flag in `CON0`. The
  receive pending is set when the bytes since the last latch reach `RXCNT`,
  so a handler that clears it without latching gets it again on every
  later byte. The timeout comes `OTCNT` × 5 cycles (at 240 MHz) after the
  last byte, and at least one byte time (320 µs). Source 20 then interrupts
  as any source does (HW-20, HW-22). E-19: with `RXCNT` 4 and `OTCNT`
  48 000, six bytes from 3 ms give a receive pending at 4.28 ms with
  `HRXCNT` 4, and a timeout at 5.92 ms with `HRXCNT` 2.
- Sources: E-19, E-20; HARNESS ("Input scripts", "Outputs").
- Standing: confirmed (E-19, E-20)

## 17. MIDI output (M6b)

### HW-72: The SMK-37's MIDI OUT, and the FM-1's
- Fact: M-VAVE's SMK-37 Pro, the FM-1's sibling keyboard, has a 3.5 mm
  MIDI OUT jack on its rear panel. It reaches an external device's MIDI IN
  through a 3.5 mm-to-MIDI adapter, so it carries serial MIDI: the MIDI 1.0
  wire format, a current loop at 31 250 baud, each byte one start bit,
  eight data bits from the least significant, one stop bit, no parity. It
  also sends MIDI over USB (a class-compliant device) and Bluetooth LE. So
  its MIDI OUT is a UART's transmit side, not USB or Bluetooth. The FM-1
  has no MIDI OUT jack (HW-67). Which UART and pin drive the SMK-37's jack,
  and how its TRS socket is wired (type A or B), the sources don't say
  (Q-20). Whether the SMK-37 has the FM-1's chip, the allowed sources don't
  say either: the emulator runs the SMK-37's own firmware on the FM-1's
  chip with a different panel, which is the emulator's view only.
- Sources: MAN (the SMK-37 Pro's manual, English part p. 3, "MIDI OUT":
  a 3.5 mm to MIDI adapter to an external device's MIDI In; Chinese part
  p. 15, USB MIDI, class-compliant; p. 16, Bluetooth; p. 17, the rear
  panel's MIDI output port); the MIDI 1.0 specification (the wire format);
  the emulator model (the SMK-37 board).
- Standing: confirmed (MAN)
- Needed by: M6b (MIDI out)

### HW-73: The UARTs' transmit side, and UART1's on the FM-1
- Fact: Each UART (HW-68) transmits as well as receives, the two sides
  independent: `BUF` for a byte at a time, and a transmit DMA from RAM,
  `TXADR` the start address and `TXCNT` (write-only) the number of bytes,
  written last. The SDK's example keeps a DMA transmit buffer 4-byte
  aligned. A transmit pending flag in `CON0` is cleared by writing bit 13
  (HW-69). On the FM-1, FM-1's own firmware sends MIDI bytes through UART1's
  transmit DMA (`TXADR` then `TXCNT`), the UART that receives the MIDI IN
  jack, although the FM-1 has no MIDI OUT jack. So a MIDI output on UART1
  shares the input's UART, its baud rate and its clock. UART1's transmit
  pin is one of PH6, PC3, PB3 or a USB pin in its fixed pairs, or any pin
  through an output channel of `JL_IOMAP` (HW-68); which, if any, the
  FM-1's board connects, the sources don't say (Q-20).
- Sources: SDK `WL82.h` lines 569-591 (`TXADR`, `TXCNT`, `BUF`); SDK
  `include_lib/driver/device/uart.h` (transmit by DMA, the transmit
  interrupt that can be left off, the transmit pin); SDK
  `apps/common/example/peripheral/uart/uart_test.c` (the DMA transmit
  buffer 4-byte aligned); SDK `include_lib/driver/cpu/wl82/asm/uart.h` (the
  pin pairs, transmit first); RE `docs/io/05-midi.md` §1 and §2.1 (FM-1's
  firmware writes UART1's transmit address and count to send MIDI; the
  transmit pending acknowledged with `0x2000`).
- Standing: confirmed (SDK, RE)
- Needed by: M6b (MIDI out)

EOF

content.content:
Speed only: a block built from RAM code is found current by the bus's
count of writes to code words, when the count hasn't changed, before
its bytes are compared with memory; upstream did so only in its wasm
build. Every write to a word a RAM block was built from is counted:
RAM's bytes are reachable only through its write methods, which count,
and the native JITs' inline stores, which send a store to a flagged word
to the bus; a block marks exactly the bytes it keeps as code. fwtest
runs without the JIT.

The F-Emulator app's patch (its 0005, emulator-patches.md section D),
taken unchanged: the added and removed lines are the app's, byte for
byte. Licensed MIT for this repository by the owner (PROVENANCE P-39).

Its crate test ram_block_sees_patched_code re-enters a RAM block after a
store patched it, interpreted and with the JIT. fwtest's outputs are
byte for byte the same with and without this patch and 0007
(docs/EMULATOR-PARITY.md). Session emulator-parity, 2026-10-24.

# The FM engine's patch format, version 1

A patch is everything the FM engine (M5, `firmware/src/fm.h`) needs to
play a sound: 112 bytes, each field one byte, or two bytes little-endian,
so a patch can be saved to flash (M7) and shared (the app) as it is,
without conversion. `tools/fm_patch.py` writes and checks patches in this
format (its `encode` and `problems`), and `fm_patch_valid()` in
`firmware/src/fm_play.c` checks them the same way. The test patches are
defined once, in `tools/fm_patch.py`, and generated into
`firmware/src/patches.c`; they are our own (R-FM-7).

## Layout

| Offset | Bytes | Field | Values |
|-------:|------:|-------|--------|
| 0 | 2 | magic | `F` `M` (0x46, 0x4D) |
| 2 | 1 | version | 1 |
| 3 | 1 | length | 112, the whole patch |
| 4 | 12 | name | printable ASCII (32 to 126), padded with 0 |
| 16 | 1 | algorithm | 1 to 10 ("The algorithms", docs/DESIGN-NOTES.md, M5) |
| 17 | 1 | feedback | 0 (none) to 7, on the algorithm's feedback operator |
| 18 | 1 | flags | bit 0: mono; the other bits 0 |
| 19 | 1 | glide | a time code (below); 0: none. Mono only |
| 20 | 1 | transpose | signed semitones, -24 to 24 |

# The FM engine's patch format, version 1

A patch is everything the FM engine (M5, `firmware/src/fm.h`) needs to
play a sound: 112 bytes, each field one byte, or two bytes little-endian,
so a patch can be saved to flash (M7) and shared (the app) as it is,
without conversion. `tools/fm_patch.py` writes and checks patches in this
format (its `encode` and `problems`), and `fm_patch_valid()` in
`firmware/src/fm_play.c` checks them the same way. The test patches are
defined once, in `tools/fm_patch.py`, and generated into
`firmware/src/patches.c`; they are our own (R-FM-7).

## Layout

| Offset | Bytes | Field | Values |
|-------:|------:|-------|--------|
| 0 | 2 | magic | `F` `M` (0x46, 0x4D) |
| 2 | 1 | version | 1 |
| 3 | 1 | length | 112, the whole patch |
| 4 | 12 | name | printable ASCII (32 to 126), padded with 0 |
| 16 | 1 | algorithm | 1 to 10 ("The algorithms", docs/DESIGN-NOTES.md, M5) |
| 17 | 1 | feedback | 0 (none) to 7, on the algorithm's feedback operator |
| 18 | 1 | flags | bit 0: mono; the other bits 0 |
| 19 | 1 | glide | a time code (below); 0: none. Mono only |
| 20 | 1 | transpose | signed semitones, -24 to 24 |
| 21 | 1 | pitch depth | signed semitones that a pitch level of 127 means, -48 to 48 |
| 22 | 3 | pitch rates | time codes: P0 to P1, P1 to P2 (then held), and to P3 on release |
| 25 | 4 | pitch levels | P0 (at note on) to P3, signed, -127 to 127 |
| 29 | 3 | reserved | 0 |
| 32 | 6 x 13 | operators | operator 1 first (below) |
| 110 | 2 | check sum | Fletcher-16 of bytes 0 to 109: low byte the first sum, high byte the second, each mod 255 |

sent is kept with the cycle its stop bit ended (Periph::midi_sent), so a
runner can capture the MIDI output: fwtest's --midi-out, and the
F-Emulator app's CoreMIDI output (harness/upstream/fm1-emu-midi-out.md).

register map and FM-1-RE's MIDI document (PROVENANCE P-41, P-43). The
harness test midi_output and the suite case midiout check it; on a board
with no MIDI OUT jack (the FM-1) the bytes go nowhere on the real device.

/* SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT */
/* SPDX-FileCopyrightText: 2026 japes98 */
/* E-21: UART1's transmit side (source 20), the MIDI output. A BUF write with the UART off
   (not sent); then the UART on with its transmit interrupt, whose handler
   counts in OUT(1) and keeps TIMER4's count and CON0 as read on entry in
   OUT(2 + 2k), OUT(3 + 2k). At the start a DMA of five bytes (a note-on,
   then a second by running status); at 3 ms a clock byte through BUF; at
   4 ms a DMA of a note-off with an active-sensing byte through BUF behind
   it. OUT(0) marks the end. */

#define UART1_CON0 REG(0x12100u)
#define UART1_BUF REG(0x1210cu)
#define UART1_TXADR REG(0x12114u)
#define UART1_TXCNT REG(0x12118u)

/* the bytes to send, in RAM (test images have no initialised data) */
#define MSG 0x01c00300u
#define OFF 0x01c00310u

p='docs/HARDWARE-SPEC.md'; s=open(p).read()
entry='''### HW-74: UART1's transmit in fwtest, and on a real FM-1
- Fact: Since fwtest 0.5.0, UART1 transmits: writing `TXCNT` sends that
  many bytes from `TXADR` (fwtest reads them from RAM at the write), and
  writing `BUF` sends one byte. Bytes go out one every 320 µs (31 250
  baud, whatever `BAUD`, `CON1`, `CLK_CON1` and the pins say), each after
  any still going, so a `BUF` byte written during a transfer goes after
  it. When the last byte has gone, `CON0` bit 15 (transmit pending) is set,
  and source 20 is raised if `CON0` bit 2 is set; writing bit 13 clears it
  (HW-69). With `CON0` bit 0 clear nothing is sent, and the bytes are
  counted in `result.json`'s `midi_out_bytes_dropped`. `--midi-out` saves
  every byte sent with the time its stop bit ended, and the MIDI messages
  they make (HARNESS, "MIDI output"). Before 0.5.0 a `TXCNT` write set the
  pending at once and sent nothing. On a real FM-1 these bytes reach no
  socket: it has no MIDI OUT jack (HW-67), and which pin, if any, its
  board gives UART1's transmit side is open (Q-20). The bit meanings are
  the emulator's (HW-70); the SMK-37's MIDI OUT is a UART's transmit side
  (HW-72), which this models for the FM-1's chip.
- Sources: E-21 (the timing, the order, the pending and its interrupt,
  nothing sent with the UART off); HARNESS ("MIDI output"); the emulator
  model with vendor patch 0009.
- Standing: confirmed (E-21)
- Needed by: M6b (MIDI out)

'''
anchor="## Open questions\n"
assert s.count(anchor)==1; s=s.replace(anchor, entry+anchor)
open(p,'w').write(s)
EOF

content.content:
## The command line

```
fwtest run IMAGE --ms MS --out DIR [options]
fwtest suite FILE --out DIR
fwtest version
```

`run` options:

| Option | What it does |
|--------|--------------|
| `--ms MS` | Run for MS emulated milliseconds (up to three decimals). Required. |
| `--out DIR` | Write the outputs here. Required; must be empty or new. |
| `--script FILE` | Timed inputs (below). |
| `--flash FILE` | The flash chip's first bytes (at most 1 MiB); the rest is erased. |
| `--ram ADDR:LEN@WHEN` | Save LEN bytes of memory at ADDR at WHEN. Numbers in decimal, or hex with `0x`. Only RAM (main RAM and the other RAM banks `HARDWARE-SPEC.md` lists) can be saved; anything else is a usage error. Repeatable. |
| `--lcd WHEN` | Save the screen as a PNG at WHEN. Repeatable. |
| `--leds-every MS` | Sample the LEDs every MS into `leds.csv`. |
| `--flash-out` | Save the whole flash chip at the end (`flash.bin`). |
| `--wav` | Save the audio output (`audio.wav`). |
| `--ipb` | Save instructions per audio block (`ipb.csv`). |
| `--console` | Save the bytes written to the chip's debug message register (`console.txt`; `HARDWARE-SPEC.md` names it). |
| `--watchdog ADDR:MS` | A hang if the 32-bit word at RAM address ADDR stays the same for more than MS ms. |
| `--halt-ok` | A halt counts as success (exit 0). |
| `--golden DIR` | Compare the outputs with the golden files in DIR (below). |

WHEN is a time in ms (`10`, `2.5`) or `end`. The run ends at `--ms`, or
earlier on a fault, halt or hang; `end` captures are taken then.

## Input scripts

## Versions

`fwtest version` prints fwtest's version and the emulator build it carries;
`result.json` has both. The image is identified by its digest. When the
harness changes, a pull request moves `config/fwtest-image` to the new
digest, so a firmware test always names the exact runner it used.

- 0.4.0: the rotate by a register and the 4-byte push and pop of any
  register list run; a dual-issue pair's head among the 4-byte ALU forms
  holds its result until after the pair ("Instructions"). The emulator is
  the F-Emulator app's but for its own raw-image loader
  (docs/EMULATOR-PARITY.md).
- 0.3.0: the block moves below a base register run, all eight modes
  of the block moves are listed (SR-7; "Instructions").
- 0.2.0: SPI1's `CON` writes set and clear bits as written ("The LCD").
- 0.1.0: the first published image.

  RAM, read at the moment of the write; writing the data register sends
  one byte. Each byte takes 320 µs on the wire (31 250 baud, whatever the
  baud and clock registers hold). A transfer started while another is
  still going waits behind it, byte for byte.

  flag is set and, if its interrupt is enabled, the UART's interrupt
  source is raised (HW-74). With the UART off nothing is sent:

  where they were sent. What breaks the rules is named: `stray-data XX`

  ...` (cut short by a status byte, or at the end).

  exactly, or with `rel-percent N` for its times; `midi-out.txt` exactly.

# Emulator parity: fwtest and the F-Emulator app

fwtest (this repository's harness) and the owner's F-Emulator app both run
the public emulator upstream, `joakimeriksson/fm1-emu`, with patches of
their own. This file lists every patch and which of the two has it, so
that a firmware behaves the same in both. Written by the spec side
(session emulator-parity, 2026-10-24); kept in general terms, as every file
outside `harness/` and `vendor/emulator/` is (CONTRIBUTING.md).

## The upstream commit

Both build on `43ed5580064885e93bc8d20be931ae950d10cd4f` (main on
2026-10-22; vendor/emulator/UPSTREAM.md), the same three crates.

## Every patch

fwtest's patches are `vendor/emulator/patches/`, applied in order by
`tools/fetch-emulator.sh`. The app's are its own branch, numbered as its
patch notes (`emulator-patches.md`, from the owner; PROVENANCE P-39) number
them, against upstream with fwtest's 0001 and 0002.

| fwtest | App | What | Kind | fwtest | App |
|--------|-----|------|------|--------|-----|
| 0001 | none | The workspace manifest lists only the three vendored crates | build | yes | not needed: only for fwtest's three-crate copy |
| 0002 | B | A write to the LCD's SPI port's control register replaces it, so its interrupt enable can be cleared (SR-3) | bug fix | yes (0.2.0) | yes (its base) |
| 0003 | none | The block moves with a register base run in all eight modes (SR-7) | bug fix | yes (0.3.0) | no: to apply (harness/upstream/fm1-emu-block-moves.md) |
| 0004 | 0003 (A) | A dual-issue pair's head among the 4-byte ALU forms with no table class holds its result until after the pair | bug fix | yes (0.4.0) | yes |
| 0005 | none | The rotate right by a register runs, as a pair's head too | gap | yes (0.4.0) | no: to apply (harness/upstream/fm1-emu-undecoded-forms.md) |
| 0006 | none | The 4-byte push and pop of any register list run, not only lists from r0 | gap | yes (0.4.0) | no: to apply (same note) |
| 0007 | 0004 (C) | Peripheral addresses looked up before the memories | speed only | yes (0.4.0) | yes |
| 0008 | 0005 (D) | Code blocks in RAM found current by a count of writes to code, on every build | speed only | yes (0.4.0) | yes |
| none | 0006 (E) | Boot a raw image | the app's loader | no: fwtest has its own (in `harness/`, docs/HARNESS.md "The raw image") | yes |
| none | not a patch | Two pattern guards rewritten so the crates build on an older Rust | build | no: fwtest builds on Rust 1.99 | yes |

fwtest 0004, 0007 and 0008 are the app's 0003, 0004 and 0005 as they
stand: their added and removed lines are byte for byte the app's, only the
line offsets refreshed for fwtest's 0003. Once the app applies fwtest's
0003, 0005 and 0006, the two are the same source but for the app's
raw-image loader and its Rust 1.94 rewrite (which, its notes say, changes
nothing that decodes). That was checked on the app's patches as the owner
dropped them, not on its branch, which this side doesn't open: on upstream
with them, fwtest's three apply with line offsets only, the crates' own
tests pass, and the core crate is then byte for byte fwtest's. fwtest's
three need nothing newer than the Rust the app builds with.

## How each was checked

- **0004 (the pair heads).** From the vendor toolchain (PROVENANCE P-40):
  its disassembler prints the second twin of each of these forms (byte 1
  `f0` / `f1`) as a pair's head, and the compiler's own code for our
  firmware relies on a pair's second half seeing the registers as they
  were before the head. fwtest's harness test runs one word of every
  family, plain and as a pair's head, and fails without the patch. The
  app's own test comes with it.
- **0005 and 0006 (the two gaps SR-7 found).** Encodings from the vendor
  assembler and disassembler; the rotate's behaviour from the compiler's
  rotate idioms, including one built with the firmware's flags in a test
  image; the lists' from the lists from r0 the compiler emits. Each has a
  harness test that fails without it (docs/HARNESS.md, "Instructions").
- **0007 and 0008 (speed only).** Taken because a test shows they change
  no behaviour. The app's test for 0007 compares the new address lookup
  with the old one at every address up to the end of the memories and a
  sweep above. For 0008 every way RAM can be written was checked to count
  as a write to code, and a harness test runs RAM code changed by stores,
  with and without the patch. Then the firmware's suite (at `cdfd067`), the
  spec experiments and the harness's own suite were run on fwtest built
  with and without 0007 and 0008: all 284 output files are byte for byte
  the same.
- **The firmware.** The same comparison between fwtest 0.3.0's emulator
  and 0.4.0's (0004 to 0008): no output of the three suites changed.

## Keeping them together

A patch that changes what the emulator does goes into both: in fwtest as a
numbered patch with a harness test that fails without it, in the app from
the note in `harness/upstream/`; this table gets a row. A speed-only patch
goes into fwtest only with a test that shows it changes nothing. When the
pinned upstream commit has a fix, both drop the patch.

# Upstream report: the block moves below a base register don't run

For the owner to file with `joakimeriksson/fm1-emu` and to apply in the
F-Emulator app. Spec side only; not filed by a session. Found in session
SR-7 (2026-10-24) against commit `43ed5580064885e93bc8d20be931ae950d10cd4f`;
our copy carries the fix as
`vendor/emulator/patches/0003-block-moves-below-the-base.patch`.

## What goes wrong

The block moves with a register base are one 4-byte family, `xm eb
<mask>` with m < 8: the base register in bits 0-3, a 16-bit register mask

# Upstream note: MIDI out from UART1's transmit side, and the app's CoreMIDI output

For the owner to apply in the F-Emulator app, and to offer to
`joakimeriksson/fm1-emu` if wanted. Spec side only; not filed by a
session. Written in session midi-in-out (2026-10-24) against commit
`43ed5580064885e93bc8d20be931ae950d10cd4f`; our copy carries the change as
`vendor/emulator/patches/0009-uart1-transmit-side.patch` (fwtest 0.5.0).
docs/EMULATOR-PARITY.md lists it.

## What upstream does

UART1 (`0x12100`) models only the MIDI IN jack's receive DMA. A write of
`TXCNT` (`0x12118`) sets the transmit pending (`CON0` bit 15) at once and
sends nothing ("no TX pin on the board"); a `BUF` (`0x1210C`) write is
plain storage. So a firmware's MIDI out vanishes, and its transmit
interrupt comes the instant it starts a transfer, not 320 µs per byte
later, which hides pacing bugs.

## What the patch does

In `fm1-soc`'s `periph.rs` and `lib.rs`:

- `TXCNT` written: `lib.rs` reads `TXCNT & 0xffff` bytes from `TXADR`
  (`0x12114`, kept in SFR storage) at that moment and hands them to
  `Periph::uart_transmit`. A `BUF` write hands over its low byte.
- `uart_transmit` drops them (counted in `midi_out_dropped()`) when
  `CON0` bit 0 is clear; otherwise it queues them behind anything still
  going. One byte goes per `midi_byte_time()` (10 bits at 31 250 baud:
  76 800 cycles at 240 MHz), whatever `BAUD` says, as the receive side
  does. `next_event` includes the transmitter, so the core never runs or
  skips past a byte's end.
- When the queue empties, `tpnd` is set and `uart_update` raises IRQ 20
  if `CON0` bit 2 is set; the existing `CON0` bit 13 write clears it.
- Every byte sent is kept as `(cycle its stop bit ended, byte)` until
  `Periph::midi_take_sent()` drains them, oldest first.

The patch applies to upstream after fwtest's 0001 to 0008 with line
offsets only; it touches no instruction decoding. fwtest's harness test
`midi_output` and the suite case `midiout` fail without it.

## The app: sending the bytes to CoreMIDI

The board each package runs on matters only for what the user is told:
the SMK-37 has a MIDI OUT jack these bytes model; a real FM-1 has none
(docs/HARDWARE-SPEC.md, HW-67, HW-72 to HW-74), so for an FM-1 package
this is the emulator's extra, and should say so in the UI.

1. **A virtual source.** At start-up, `MIDIClientCreateWithBlock`, then
   `MIDISourceCreateWithProtocol` (`kMIDIProtocol_1_0`) named, say, "FM-1
   Emulator MIDI Out", so a DAW or another synth can pick it as an input.
   Give it a stable `kMIDIPropertyUniqueID` (saved in the app's
   preferences) so DAWs keep the routing across launches.
2. **Drain every frame.** After each slice of emulation, call
   `soc.periph.midi_take_sent()`. Never let the bytes pile up: the
   emulator keeps them only until taken.
3. **Bytes to messages.** CoreMIDI wants whole messages: parse the byte
   stream as MIDI 1.0 does, keeping the running status, passing real-time
   bytes (`F8` to `FF`) on at once even inside another message, and
   collecting system exclusive from `F0` to `F7` (a status byte other than
   real-time ends it unterminated: drop it). fwtest's decoder,
   `harness/src/midi.rs` (MIT, ours, no emulator code), does exactly this
   and can be ported; its tests list the edge cases. Expand running status
   into full messages before sending.
4. **Times.** Each byte's cycle is emulated time at 240 MHz. Keep one
   anchor, the host time (`mach_absolute_time()`) and emulated cycle when
   emulation (re)starts or the user changes speed; a message's host time is
   `anchor_host + (cycle - anchor_cycle) / 240e6` seconds, converted with
   `mach_timebase_info`, plus a fixed latency (say 5 ms) so messages
   scheduled from a frame already in the past still go out evenly. If
   emulation runs slower than real time, or a computed time is already
   past, send with timestamp 0 (now) rather than late-stamped.
5. **Send.** Build a `MIDIEventList` with `MIDIEventListInit` and
   `MIDIEventListAdd`, one MIDI 1.0 UMP per channel message (system
   exclusive as UMP data packets of up to six bytes each), and
   `MIDIReceivedEventList` on the virtual source. On macOS before 11,
   the `MIDIPacketList` and `MIDIReceived` calls do the same with the
   bytes as they are.
6. **Panic on stop.** When emulation stops, pauses, resets or loads
   another package mid-note, send note-off for every note the stream left
   on (track note-ons per channel and key as you parse), or `B0+n 7B 00`
   (all notes off) on each channel used, so nothing downstream hangs.

## Checking it

Run the harness test image `harness/tests/images/midiout.bin` in the app
with the output connected to a MIDI monitor (MIDI Monitor, or a DAW's MIDI
input view): two note-ons on channel 1 (60 and 62), a clock, a note-off
for 60 and an active-sensing byte, as `harness/tests/golden/midiout/
midi-out.txt` lists them, the five at 0.96, 1.6, 3.32, 4.96 and 5.28 ms
after start.

`TXCNT` (`0x12118`) sets the transmit pending (`CON0` bit 15) at once and
sends nothing ("no TX pin on the board"); a `BUF` (`0x1210C`) write is
plain storage. So a firmware's MIDI out vanishes, and its transmit
interrupt comes the instant it starts a transfer, not 320 µs per byte
later, which hides pacing bugs.

In `fm1-soc`'s `periph.rs` and `lib.rs`:

- `TXCNT` written: `lib.rs` reads `TXCNT & 0xffff` bytes from `TXADR`
  (`0x12114`, kept in SFR storage) at that moment and hands them to
  `Periph::uart_transmit`. A `BUF` write hands over its low byte.
- `uart_transmit` drops them (counted in `midi_out_dropped()`) when
  `CON0` bit 0 is clear; otherwise it queues them behind anything still
  going. One byte goes per `midi_byte_time()` (10 bits at 31 250 baud:
  76 800 cycles at 240 MHz), whatever `BAUD` says, as the receive side
  does. `next_event` includes the transmitter, so the core never runs or
  skips past a byte's end.

  if `CON0` bit 2 is set; the existing `CON0` bit 13 write clears it.

the SMK-37 has a MIDI OUT jack these bytes model; a real FM-1 has none

   preferences) so DAWs keep the routing across launches.
2. **Drain every frame.** After each slice of emulation, call
   `soc.periph.midi_take_sent()`. Never let the bytes pile up: the
   emulator keeps them only until taken.
3. **Bytes to messages.** CoreMIDI wants whole messages: parse the byte
   stream as MIDI 1.0 does, keeping the running status, passing real-time

   another package mid-note, send note-off for every note the stream left

it into a pull request (the owner chose an issue over letting
      workflows open pull requests).
    - **The job:** `audit.yml` runs JPlag 6.3.0 (pinned by hash, in a Java
      image pinned by digest) on our firmware and the control
      (pico-examples at sdk-2.2.0), with the SDK as base code.
    - **The gate:** a pair fails above the control's longest match plus
      24 tokens. The longest match was chosen by a calibration between two
      unrelated permissive projects: chance runs stay at 33 tokens or
      below, while the ratio reaches 0.857.
    - **Isolation:** the targets exist only in a job with no secrets, and
      only scores and file names reach the record
      (`records/<sha>/audit/`).
    - **First run** (the merge `362480c8`, docs/AUDIT.md "The first run"):
      PASS in under 4 minutes, so pushes run the full set. 516 targets,
      18,498 files; the control's baseline was 35 tokens (threshold 59), no
      target was control-related, and our best pair was a 12-token match.
      Its report is in the record, beside the main record.
    - **The self-test gap** (2026-10-23, a spec session; docs/AUDIT.md,
      "The self-test gap"). From M2's firmware on, the self-test failed
      with "8 of our 9 files found". The file was `src/font.c`, a single
      table JPlag makes 5 tokens of, so it drops it as `TOO_SMALL`. In
      these runs the gate passed, but `src/font.c` was compared with
      nothing. The merges that ran without a passing self-test:
      - #34, #35 and #36: their own audit runs were cancelled while
        queued. #37's run covered their commits;
      - #37 (run 39877916755), #40 (run 39886734506) and #45 (run
        39888000310): self-test FAIL, gate PASS.

      Those runs stay red in the records. **The fix:** a file JPlag cannot
      score is reported as "not scorable by JPlag", with the reason, and
      goes to a text check (C-AUDIT-TEXT). That check finds exact copies,
      and the share of the file's normalised text in each target file, and
      fails at 0.5. The threshold is calibrated on the same permissive
      pair as the gate. The self-test now also finds a reformatted copy of
      each file, so it covers the text check too.
  - **Auditor role**: CONTRIBUTING.md, `config/claude/auditor.json`,
    `tools/auditor-setup.sh`. Its transcripts go to the owner's private
    repository (created when the first auditor session runs), never here.
    None has run.
  - No spec requests were open.

    each core, allocation and click-free stealing; mono with legato and
    glide; a versioned patch format (docs/PATCH-FORMAT.md) and nine test
    patches of our own; minimal controls (PRESETS, ALGORITHM, KNOB1 to
    KNOB4, SEL with MONO/POLY). R-FM-1 to R-FM-9.
  - **Tests**: FM sidebands within 0.002 dB of the Bessel functions;
    envelope stages within 0.9 ms; glides within 0.05 semitones; velocity
    within 0.03 dB; stealing without a click; 11 s of the heaviest input on
    all 16 voices without an underrun; identical output on two runs;
    golden WAVs for every test patch.
  - **Figures** (fwtest): about 24 instructions an operator-sample; at
    rest 1 803 a block; loaded 84 918 (24% of core 0; core 1 about 22%);
    about 37 six-operator voices a core would fit, 16 ship, a margin of
    four times for the chip. Code 15 696 bytes, static RAM 142 008, stack
    388 (the M5 budgets, #69).
  - **Spec request SR-7** (#68): fwtest doesn't run a two-register load
    the compiler emits; a short, documented workaround until it does.
  - **The similarity audit** passes on #70's commit (no pair flagged,
    no text match). Its self-test has failed on every main commit since
    #61 (it finds 25 of our 30 files in its made-up copy; the Plaits
    demo's small files are the likely misses): the owner decides who fixes
    it (the audit's tooling is the spec side's, SR-4).
  - **Next: M6, MIDI in.** The engine already takes notes with velocity
    (`fm_note_on`); M6 needs UART1 and the MIDI jack from the spec side
    (Q-12).

## Risks

- **The toolchain's availability and terms.** JieLi's Linux toolchain has no
  licence file (docs/TOOLCHAIN.md). We never redistribute it. If the
  download disappears, a full rebuild needs another copy (the private
  preservation repo), but every released binary stays verifiable by its
  recorded hash. The vendor's short link already points at a newer release
  (20260730.1) than the pinned one; the pinned file is fetched by its direct
  URL.
- **Packages for real hardware.** A `.fwsc` package may need M-VAVE's boot or
  update loader, which we can't redistribute. Find out from FM-1-RE's
  documents only, before M9, and record the answer here. The app is
  unaffected (it can boot our raw image). *Answer: not yet investigated.*
- **The emulator doesn't model USB**, so M11 is hardware-only.
- **Merge signatures are GitHub's.** Since 2026-10-22 the owner merges with
  GitHub's button, so merge commits are signed by GitHub (`web-flow`) and the
  owner's identity rests on GitHub's `merged_by` record, checked by C-MERGE.
  Milestone tags carry the owner's own SSH signature. The first merge's
  record shows C-MERGE FAIL under the earlier rule (CONTRIBUTING.md, "Merge
  policy and its history").

    (`fm_note_on`); M6 needs UART1 and the MIDI jack from the spec side
    (Q-12).

## Risks

- **The toolchain's availability and terms.** JieLi's Linux toolchain has no
  licence file (docs/TOOLCHAIN.md). We never redistribute it. If the
  download disappears, a full rebuild needs another copy (the private
  preservation repo), but every released binary stays verifiable by its
  recorded hash. The vendor's short link already points at a newer release
  (20260730.1) than the pinned one; the pinned file is fetched by its direct
  URL.
- **Packages for real hardware.** A `.fwsc` package may need M-VAVE's boot or
  update loader, which we can't redistribute. Find out from FM-1-RE's
  documents only, before M9, and record the answer here. The app is
  unaffected (it can boot our raw image). *Answer: not yet investigated.*
- **The emulator doesn't model USB**, so M11 is hardware-only.
- **Merge signatures are GitHub's.** Since 2026-10-22 the owner merges with
  GitHub's button, so merge commits are signed by GitHub (`web-flow`) and the
  owner's identity rests on GitHub's `merged_by` record, checked by C-MERGE.
  Milestone tags carry the owner's own SSH signature. The first merge's
  record shows C-MERGE FAIL under the earlier rule (CONTRIBUTING.md, "Merge
  policy and its history").

def reformat(text):
    """A near-exact copy for the self-test: no comments, each line
    re-indented, and a comment of its own at the top, so the bytes differ."""
    text = LITERAL_OR_COMMENT.sub(lambda m: m.group(0) if m.group(0)[0] in "\"'" else " ", text)
    lines = ["\t" + line.strip() if not line.lstrip().startswith("#") else line.strip()
             for line in text.splitlines() if line.strip()]
    return "/* reformatted */\n" + "\n".join(lines) + "\n"


def selftest_target(work_parent, cfg):
    """A made-up local target: verbatim and reformatted copies of our files
    and one unrelated file, in a git repository served by path. Returns
    (target dict, its folder)."""
    d = tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="audit-selftest-", dir=work_parent)
    src = os.path.join(ROOT, cfg["ours"])
    for dirpath, _, files in os.walk(src):
        for f in files:
            if wanted(f, cfg["suffixes"]):
                rel = os.path.relpath(os.path.join(dirpath, f), src)
                os.makedirs(os.path.join(d, "copied", os.path.dirname(rel)), exist_ok=True)
                shutil.copyfile(os.path.join(dirpath, f), os.path.join(d, "copied", rel))
                os.makedirs(os.path.join(d, "reformatted", os.path.dirname(rel)), exist_ok=True)
                with open(os.path.join(dirpath, f), encoding="utf-8") as fin, \
                        open(os.path.join(d, "reformatted", rel), "w", encoding="utf-8") as fout:
                    fout.write(reformat(fin.read()))
    with open(os.path.join(d, "unrelated.c"), "w") as f:
        f.write("int unrelated(int a) { return a * 3 + 1; }\n")
    env = dict(GIT_ENV, GIT_AUTHOR_NAME="t", GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL="[REDACTED:email]",
               GIT_COMMITTER_NAME="t", GIT_COMMITTER_EMAIL="[REDACTED:email]")
    for args in (["init", "-q"], ["add", "-A"], ["commit", "-q", "-m", "selftest"],
                 ["config", "uploadpack.allowFilter", "true"], ["config", "uploadpack.allowAnySHA1InWant", "true"]):
        subprocess.run(["git"] + args, cwd=d, check=True, stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.PIPE, env=env)
    commit = git(["rev-parse", "HEAD"], d).stdout.decode().strip()
    tree = git(["rev-parse", "HEAD^{tree}"], d).stdout.decode().strip()
    return {"repo": "selftest/copy-of-ours", "url": "file://" + d, "commit": commit, "tree": tree,
            "status": "scored", "licence_class": "none"}, d


def selftest_verdict(report, cfg):
    """Every one of our files must be found in the made-up target, and the
    report written. A file JPlag scored: by a match covering at least 90% of
    its tokens. A file JPlag cannot score: by the text check, as an exact copy
    (the verbatim one) and at or above its threshold without being exact (the
    reformatted one). A file JPlag scored but matched nowhere fails."""
    files = report.get("ours_files", [])
    tokens = {f["file"]: f["tokens"] for f in files if f["state"] == "scored"}
    best = {}
    for o, p, l, m, v in report.get("selftest", {}).get("ours_best", []):
        best[o] = max(best.get(o, 0), l)
    by_jplag = [f for f, t in tokens.items() if best.get(f, 0) >= 0.9 * t]
    exact, near = set(), set()
    for o, path, c, is_exact in report.get("selftest", {}).get("text", []):
        if is_exact:
            exact.add(o)
        elif c >= cfg["text_check"]["threshold"]:
            near.add(o)
    by_text = [f["file"] for f in files if "not_scorable" in f and f["file"] in exact & near]
    leak_ok = any(c["id"] == "C-AUDIT-LEAK" and c["result"] == "PASS" for c in report.get("checks", []))
    found = len(by_jplag) + len(by_text)
    ok = bool(files) and found == len(files) and leak_ok
    return ok, "%d of our %d files found in a target holding copies of them (%d by JPlag, %d by the text check); " \
        "leak check %s" % (found, len(files), len(by_jplag), len(by_text), "PASS" if leak_ok else "not passed")


def check_artifact(folder):
    names = sorted(os.listdir(folder))
    if names != ["report.json", "report.md"]:
        return ["unexpected files: %s" % names]
    problems = []
    for n in names:
        if os.path.getsize(os.path.join(folder, n)) > 2 << 20:
            problems.append("%s is too large" % n)
    r = load_json(os.path.join(folder, "report.json"))
    if r.get("schema") != SCHEMA or not isinstance(r.get("checks"), list):
        problems.append("report.json is not an audit report")
    return problems


def main(argv=None):
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("command", choices=["run", "selftest", "check-artifact"])

                    with open(os.path.join(work, sub, "base", "b%d" % j, rel), "wb") as fh:
                        fh.write(data)
            code = run_jplag(cfg, work, sub)
            result = os.path.join(work, sub, "result.jplag")
            if code or not os.path.exists(result):
                raise RuntimeError("JPlag failed (exit %d); its log is not shown, as it can quote the files" % code)
            pairs, f_i, t_i = read_results(result)
            os.remove(result)
            s_i = score(pairs, cfg, pool.where)
            failed.update({n: v for n, v in f_i.items() if n in mine or (i == 0 and n in control)})
            tokens.update({n: v for n, v in t_i.items() if n in mine or (i == 0 and n in control)})
            # A file JPlag could not score at all goes to the text check

            unscorable_i = {n: read_ours(n) for n in sorted(mine) if n in f_i}

            if s is None:

        # and the control scored again under it (since SR-4).
        tc = cfg["text_check"]
        failed, tokens, text, s, report["passes"] = {}, {}, [], None, []
        for i, (label, mine, tr) in enumerate(passes):
            sub = "g%d" % i
            for d in ("new", "base"):
                os.makedirs(os.path.join(work, sub, d))
            for n in list(mine) + list(control):
                shutil.copyfile(os.path.join(work, "new", n), os.path.join(work, sub, "new", n))
            for j, (b, files) in enumerate(tr, 1):
                for rel, data in files.items():
                    os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(os.path.join(work, sub, "base", "b%d" % j, rel)), exist_ok=True)
                    with open(os.path.join(work, sub, "base", "b%d" % j, rel), "wb") as fh:
                        fh.write(data)
            code = run_jplag(cfg, work, sub)
            result = os.path.join(work, sub, "result.jplag")
            if code or not os.path.exists(result):
                raise RuntimeError("JPlag failed (exit %d); its log is not shown, as it can quote the files" % code)
            pairs, f_i, t_i = read_results(result)
            os.remove(result)
            s_i = score(pairs, cfg, pool.where)
            failed.update({n: v for n, v in f_i.items() if n in mine or (i == 0 and n in control)})
            tokens.update({n: v for n, v in t_i.items() if n in mine or (i == 0 and n in control)})
            # A file JPlag could not score at all goes to the text check
            # instead, with the same base code; a file it scored that matched
            # nothing ("no match") does not.
            unscorable_i = {n: read_ours(n) for n in sorted(mine) if n in f_i}
            if unscorable_i:
                text += text_scores(unscorable_i, pool.dir, tc["k"], [d for _, f in tr for d in f.values()])
            report["passes"].append({"files": label, "count": len(mine), "base_code": [b["path"] for b, _ in tr],
                                     "control_max_tokens": s_i["control_max"], "threshold_tokens": s_i["threshold"],
                                     "control_related": s_i["related"]})
            if s is None:
                s = s_i
            else:
                s["ours"] = sorted(s["ours"] + s_i["ours"], key=lambda x: (-x[2], -x[3], x[0], x[1]))
                s["ours_control"] = sorted(s["ours_control"] + s_i["ours_control"],
                                           key=lambda x: (-x[2], -x[3], x[0], x[1]))
                s["flagged"] = sorted(s["flagged"] + s_i["flagged"], key=lambda x: (-x[2], -x[3], x[0], x[1]))
                s["related_extra"] = s.get("related_extra", []) + [s_i["related"]]
            shutil.rmtree(os.path.join(work, sub), ignore_errors=True)
        text.sort(key=lambda x: (-x[3], -x[2], x[0], x[1]))
        names = dict(ours)
        names.update(control)
        # JPlag leaves a file that matched nothing (no run of min_tokens) out
        # of its index, so its token count is unknown; it was still compared.
        report["ours_files"] = [{"file": p, "tokens": tokens.get(n), "state": failed.get(n, "scored" if n in tokens else "no match")}
                                for n, p in sorted(ours.items())]
        unscorable = sorted(n for n in ours if n in failed)
        for f, n in zip(report["ours_files"], sorted(ours)):
            if n in failed:
                f["not_scorable"] = not_scorable(failed[n], cfg)
        text_flagged = [x for x in text if x[3] or x[2] >= tc["threshold"]]
        best_text = {}
        for x in text:
            best_text.setdefault(x[0], x)
        report["text_check"] = {"k": tc["k"], "threshold": tc["threshold"], "files": [ours[n] for n in unscorable],
                                "best": [text_row(best_text[n], ours, pool.where, licences) if n in best_text else
                                         {"ours": ours[n], "containment": 0.0, "exact": False, "target_files": [],
                                          "target_places": 0} for n in unscorable],
                                "top_pairs": [text_row(x, ours, pool.where, licences) for x in text[:cfg["top_pairs"]]],
                                "flagged": [text_row(x, ours, pool.where, licences, limit=None) for x in text_flagged]}
        text_check = ("FAIL" if text_flagged else "PASS",
                                  ("%d of our files not scorable by JPlag (%s), compared as text with %d target files; "
                                   "%d pairs an exact copy or at or above %.2f of %d-character pieces"
                                   % (len(unscorable), ", ".join(ours[n] for n in unscorable), len(pool.where),
                                      len(text_flagged), tc["threshold"], tc["k"])) if unscorable else
                                  "every file of ours was scored by JPlag; none needed the text check")
        report["control_max_tokens"] = s["control_max"]
        report["threshold_tokens"] = s["threshold"]
        report["top_pairs"] = [pair_row(x, ours, pool.where, licences) for x in s["ours"][:cfg["top_pairs"]]]
        report["control_top_pairs"] = [pair_row(x, control, pool.where, licences) for x in s["control"][:5]]
        report["ours_vs_control_best"] = ([{"ours": ours.get(x[0]), "control": control.get(x[1]), "longest_tokens": x[2],
                                            "max": round(x[3], 4)} for x in s["ours_control"][:3]])
        by_repo_ours, by_repo_ctl = {}, s["control_per_target"]
        for x in s["ours"]:
            for r, _ in pool.where.get(x[1], []):
                by_repo_ours[r] = max(by_repo_ours.get(r, 0), x[2])

cd ~/Development/[REDACTED:private]/spec && git push -q -u origin spec/midi-out-harness 2>&1 | grep -v '^remote' ; gh pr create -B main -H spec/midi-out-harness -t "harness: MIDI out, the UART's transmit side and --midi-out (fwtest 0.5.0)" -F - <<'EOF' 2>&1 | tail -1
**What:**
- **Vendor patch 0009** models the MIDI input UART's transmit side.
  - A DMA write or a single-byte write sends bytes one every 320 µs, queued behind any still going.
  - The transmit pending flag, and its interrupt, come when the last byte has gone.
  - Nothing is sent while the UART is off.
- **fwtest 0.5.0** adds `--midi-out`:
  - `midi-out.csv`: each byte with the time its stop bit ended.
  - `midi-out.txt`: the MIDI messages, decoded by the MIDI 1.0 rules (running status, real-time bytes, sysex, rule breaks named).
  - Both can be golden files.
  - `result.json` gains `midi_out_bytes_dropped`.
- **HW-74** says what fwtest does, and that a real FM-1 has no socket for these bytes.
- **Docs:** HARNESS.md gets a "MIDI output" section. EMULATOR-PARITY.md lists 0009. `harness/upstream/fm1-emu-midi-out.md` tells the app how to send the bytes to CoreMIDI.

**Why:** the owner's MIDI-out task, part (b), for M6b. R-HARN-3, R-SPEC-4.

**How:**
- The transmit side comes from the SDK's UART register map and its own UART output, plus FM-1-RE's MIDI document.
- The timing comes from the MIDI wire format, as on the receive side. The decoder is our own.
- The emulator keeps sent bytes only until the runner drains them, so the app's long runs don't grow in memory.

**Result:**
- **Tests:** the harness tests pass, including the new `midi_output` test and the decoder's tests; so do the emulator crates' own tests.
- **Goldens:** the harness suite and every spec experiment (E-21 is new) match their golden files.
- **Firmware suite** (at `1537391`): the same 176 files on 0.4.0 and 0.5.0, except the version and the new field.
- **Patch:** applies to upstream from scratch.
- **Checks:** check-hardware-spec, check-emulator-terms and check-private pass; unit tests 287 OK.

/*
 * SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
 * SPDX-FileCopyrightText: 2026 japes98
 *
 * The audio layer (M4): the output, double-buffered and driven by its
 * interrupt, and the one callback a sound engine implements. This is the
 * API engines are written against, beside input.h; keep it small and
 * stable (docs/DESIGN-NOTES.md, M4, "The audio API").
 *
 * - The engine is one function, audio_engine_fn. The audio layer calls it
 *   once a block, from the output's interrupt, to fill the half of the
 *   buffer that has just finished playing while the other half plays.
 * - A block is AUDIO_FRAMES stereo frames: 2 * AUDIO_FRAMES words, left
 *   then right, each a 24-bit signed sample, sign-extended to 32 bits,
 *   within -AUDIO_FULL .. AUDIO_FULL (HW-44). The engine writes them
 *   straight into the buffer the output plays from: nothing is copied or
 *   converted after it, so it must write every word and stay in range.
 * - The rate is AUDIO_RATE_NUM / AUDIO_RATE_DEN frames a second (HW-45):
 *   44 117.647 Hz, not 44 100.
 * - Between blocks the engine reads the panel's input events with
 *   input_read_audio() (input.h), from inside its callback: the same
 *   events, in the same order, as main's input_read(), from a queue of
 *   their own. input_value() gives any control's present state.
 * - The callback runs in an interrupt at the lowest priority: the tick
 *   and the input scan may interrupt it, main never does. It must finish
 *   within one block (AUDIO_FRAMES / rate, 1.451 ms); a block it is late
 *   for is an underrun, counted and reported on the debug channel
 *   (sb_audio.underruns).
 */

#ifndef AUDIO_H
#define AUDIO_H

#include "sb.h"

#define AUDIO_FRAMES     64u           /* stereo frames a block */
#define AUDIO_RATE_NUM   24000000u     /* frames a second: 24 MHz / 544 (HW-45) */
#define AUDIO_RATE_DEN   544u
#define AUDIO_FULL       0x7FFFFF      /* 24-bit full scale */

/* Fills frames stereo frames at out: out[2n] left, out[2n + 1] right. */
typedef void (*audio_engine_fn)(s32 *out, u32 frames);

/* Starts the output with silence and engine as its engine; main calls it
 * once, before interrupts are on. */
void audio_start(audio_engine_fn engine);
void audio_block(void) __attribute__((interrupt("")));

/* The audio record: counters, at a fixed place in RAM right after the
 * input record (firmware/app.ld), for the tests to capture with fwtest's
 * --ram (tools/fw-suite.py reads this layout). Times are in time base
 * ticks (24 a microsecond). */
#define AUDIO_MARKER     0x34445541u   /* "AUD4" in memory order */
struct sb_audio_record {
    u32 marker;       /* AUDIO_MARKER once the output runs */
    u32 start;        /* sb_ticks() when the output started */
    u32 blocks;       /* blocks the engine filled */
    u32 underruns;    /* blocks it was late for, or a half that went by */
    u32 fill_last;    /* the last block's fill: interrupt to engine done */
    u32 fill_max;     /* the longest */
    u32 dropped;      /* input events the engine's queue dropped (full) */
    u32 engine[9];    /* the engine's own (SYNTH_* below) */
};
extern volatile struct sb_audio_record sb_audio;

/* What the engine keeps in sb_audio.engine: M4's test instrument's
 * fields, kept by the FM engine since M5 (fm_play.c). */
#define SYNTH_VOICES_ON  0   /* voices sounding */
#define SYNTH_NOTES      1   /* notes started */
#define SYNTH_TONE       2   /* 1 while the test tone plays */
#define SYNTH_MASTER     3   /* the MASTER gain, 0 to 1 << 24 */
#define SYNTH_EVENTS     4   /* input events taken */
#define SYNTH_STOLEN     5   /* notes that took a voice still sounding */
#define SYNTH_OCTAVE     6   /* octave shift, -2 to 2, as stored (s32) */
#define SYNTH_FIRST_ON   7   /* sb_audio.blocks when the first note began */
#define SYNTH_LAST_OFF   8   /* sb_audio.blocks when a voice last went silent */


#endif

### The self-test gap (M2 to the text check)

From the merge of #35 (M2's firmware, which added `src/font.c`) until the
text check, every push's self-test failed: "8 of our 9 files found". The
file not found was `src/font.c`, which JPlag drops as `TOO_SMALL` (above).
The gate's own checks passed in each of those runs, but `src/font.c` was
compared with nothing. Those runs stay red in the records; docs/PLAN.md
lists them.

## When the audit fails

Nobody on the spec side or the firmware side opens the matched code, or the
target, to see what matched.

1. **The owner is told.** The failed `audit` run and its report say which
   of our files, which target files (by name) and what scores. Whoever
   sees it first tells the owner, and repeats nothing beyond those names
   and numbers.
2. **The owner starts an auditor session** (CONTRIBUTING.md, "Roles"):
   - in a folder of its own, set up with `tools/auditor-setup.sh
     ~/<top>/auditor`, which installs `config/claude/auditor.json`;
   - it adds its entry to docs/EXPOSURE.md before anything else;
   - the auditor reads only the flagged pairs: our file, and the target
     file at its pinned commit.
3. **The auditor writes a finding** in `audit/findings/`, in general terms
   only: which of our files, the target's repository and path, the scores,
   and the conclusion. Possible conclusions are coincidence, a common
   source (the SDK, a datasheet's sequence, a standard idiom), or derived.
   It contains no target code and no description of the target's
   structure. The finding comes by pull request, reviewed by the owner.
4. **Then:**
   - *Coincidence or a common source:* the pair goes in
     `audit/accepted.json`, with our file, the target's repository and path,
     the accepted longest match and the finding. A higher score later fails
     again.
   - *Derived:* the owner decides how the firmware side replaces our file
     clean-room, from HARDWARE-SPEC.md, without the finding's details.
5. **The auditor is done for good.** It never writes firmware or spec
   afterwards, in any session.

p='docs/AUDIT.md'; s=open(p).read()
anchor="""compared with nothing. Those runs stay red in the records; docs/PLAN.md
lists them.
"""
new=anchor+"""
### The second self-test gap (#61 to the similarity rule)

From the merge of #61 (M4b's Plaits demo) the self-test failed again: "23
of our 27 files found", then "25 of our 30" from #70 on (session
midi-in-out, 2026-10-24, found why by running it locally):

- **Four of the demo's files** (`plaits_demo.c`, `plaits_voice.cc`,
  `sftest.c`, `runtime/softfloat.c`) were matched in full by their copies
  (JPlag's similarity 1.0), but in pieces: JPlag leaves out what matches
  the Plaits base code, which splits a verbatim copy's match, so the
  longest piece stayed under 90% of the file's tokens.
- **`src/audio.h`** matched nothing, not even its own verbatim copy
  (state "no match"), and such a file went nowhere: JPlag doesn't cover
  it, and the text check took only files JPlag could not score.

**The fix:** a file JPlag scored is found by a match covering 90% of its
tokens, or by a similarity of at least 0.9 with a copy of itself (the
report now names each pair's target file, so another file's copy doesn't
count). A file JPlag matched with nothing goes to the text check too, in
the real audit as well, so every file is covered by JPlag or by the text
check; the report says which, and why. The self-test then finds 30 of 30
(26 by JPlag, 4 by the text check). On the real audit at `1537391`, five
of our files matched nothing (three headers, `src/start.c`, the demo's
`plaits_voice.h`); they are now compared as text too. The gate and the
text check passed in every one of these runs; the runs stay red in the
records, and docs/PLAN.md lists them.
"""
assert s.count(anchor)==1; s=s.replace(anchor,new)
s=s.replace("### The self-test gap (M2 to the text check)","### The self-test gap (M2 to the text check)",1)
open(p,'w').write(s)
EOF
